newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee considering fate of tobacco business.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee considering fate of tobacco business.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp will consider the future of a small tobacco business that is based in Europe, which accounts for about two percent of its annual sales.
"It's under consideration," Chairman John Bryan told reporters after the annual meeting.
But he declined to say if Sara Lee will divest the tobacco operation, which consists of a cut tobacco business that is integrated with its Douwe Egberts coffee and tea business in Europe.
Bryan said only "a tiny bit" of the tobacco product is sold in the United States.
Sara Lee's total net sales for fiscal 1996, ended last June, were $18.6 billion.

Among Sara Lee's other businesses, Bryan said the company is looking to build its direct-marketing network for selling personal care and other products, particularly in developing economies such as Mexico, Indonesia, the Philippine, Uruguay and South Africa.
He said discussions are going on for possible acquisitions to build the direct-marketing business in Latin America and Asia, including Japan.
